assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Frequency, f
items.clue: The number of complete oscillations per unit time.

items.label: Displacement, x
items.clue: The distance of the oscillating body from its equilibrium position, in a stated direction.

items.label: Amplitude, x₀
items.clue: The maximum displacement of the oscillating body from its equilibrium position: the distance from equilibrium to either extreme.

items.label: Simple harmonic motion (SHM)
items.clue: Oscillation in which the acceleration of a body is proportional to its displacement from a fixed equilibrium position and is always directed towards that position.

questions.stem: A body is displaced from its equilibrium position and released. Which condition ensures that it then moves with simple harmonic motion?

options.text: A resultant force of constant size acts on it, directed towards the equilibrium position.
The resultant force on it is proportional to its displacement and acts in the same direction as it.
It moves back and forth along the same path, taking the same time for each cycle.
The resultant force on it is proportional to its displacement and directed towards equilibrium.

questions.explanation: This is the condition for SHM. The size of the resultant force is proportional to the displacement from equilibrium, and its direction is always towards equilibrium, so a = −ω²x.

questions.stem: The defining equation of simple harmonic motion is a = −ω²x. What is the significance of the minus sign?

options.text: The body is slowing down at every point of its motion, as its acceleration is negative.
The oscillation is losing energy, so its amplitude gradually decreases as time passes.
The acceleration always points opposite to the displacement, towards the equilibrium position.
The acceleration of the body points in the negative direction throughout the motion.

questions.explanation: ω² is positive, so the minus sign makes a and x opposite in sign at every instant. Whichever side of equilibrium the body is on, its acceleration points back towards equilibrium.

questions.stem: A particle moves with simple harmonic motion. Which statement about the quantities used to describe its motion is correct?

options.text: The amplitude is greatest at each extreme and zero when the particle is at equilibrium.
The equilibrium position is where the particle is momentarily at rest in each cycle.
Displacement is measured from equilibrium and is negative for half of each cycle.
The time period is the time taken to move from one extreme to the other.

questions.explanation: Displacement is measured from equilibrium and is signed. The particle spends half of each cycle on each side of equilibrium, so its displacement is positive for half the cycle and negative for the other half.

questions.stem: A body moving with simple harmonic motion passes through its equilibrium position 40 times in 12.0 s. What is its angular frequency?
questions.explanation: The body passes equilibrium twice per oscillation, so 40 passes are 20 oscillations: T = 12.0/20 = 0.600 s. ω = 2π/T = 2π/0.600 = 10.5 rad s⁻¹.

questions.stem: A trolley hung from a newton meter gives a reading of 14.7 N. The trolley is then attached to a spring system on a horizontal track and oscillates with negligible friction. The spring constant of the system is 7.50 N m⁻¹. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the time period of the oscillation?
The time period of a simple pendulum is given by T = 2π√(l/g). Which condition must be met for this equation to give an accurate value?

options.text: The amplitude can be of any size, since the period is independent of the amplitude.
The bob must be light, as a heavier bob is pulled harder and swings faster than predicted.
The bob swings with a regular period, which makes its motion simple harmonic.
The amplitude is small, so the restoring force is close to proportional to displacement.

questions.stem: A mass on a horizontal spring moves with simple harmonic motion on a frictionless surface; air resistance is negligible. Which statement about the energy of the oscillator is correct?

options.text: At each extreme, E_k is greatest, because the acceleration of the mass is greatest there.
At each extreme, the total energy is zero, because the mass is not moving there.
At each extreme, all the energy is stored in the spring, because the mass is at rest.
The total energy falls during each cycle, because energy is used up in keeping the mass moving.

questions.stem: Each option describes a body that can move along a straight line. It gives the resultant force F on the body when it is held at displacements x = +0.020 m, +0.040 m and +0.060 m from its equilibrium position, in that order. At the corresponding negative displacements, F has the same size and the opposite sign. Which body will move with simple harmonic motion when displaced and released?

A body moves with simple harmonic motion along a horizontal line with angular frequency 4.0 rad s⁻¹. Displacements to the right of the equilibrium position are positive. The body is released from rest 0.050 m to the right of the equilibrium position. What is its acceleration when it has moved 0.020 m from the point of release?

A glider on a horizontal air track moves with simple harmonic motion alongside a metre rule. It moves back and forth between the 0.20 m mark and the 0.60 m mark on the rule. What are the amplitude and the equilibrium position of the motion?

options.text: Amplitude 0.20 m; equilibrium position at the 0.40 m mark
Amplitude 0.40 m; equilibrium position at the 0.40 m mark
Amplitude 0.60 m; equilibrium position at the 0.40 m mark
Amplitude 0.40 m; equilibrium position at the 0.20 m mark

questions.explanation: The equilibrium position is midway between the extremes, at the 0.40 m mark. The amplitude is the maximum displacement from there: 0.60 − 0.40 = 0.20 m.

questions.stem: A mass hanging from a spring oscillates with simple harmonic motion with an angular frequency of 40.0 rad s⁻¹. What is the time period of the oscillation?
questions.explanation: One oscillation corresponds to 2π rad of phase, so T = 2π/ω = 2π/40.0 = 0.157 s. Equivalently f = ω/2π = 6.37 Hz and T = 1/f = 0.157 s.

questions.stem: A body on a spring oscillates with time period T and amplitude A. It is replaced by a body of four times the mass, which is set oscillating on the same spring with amplitude 2A. What happens to the time period?

options.text: It quadruples, as T is proportional to m and does not depend on the amplitude.
It halves, as T depends on √(k/m), so a larger mass shortens the period.
It doubles, as T depends on √m and does not depend on the amplitude.
It is unchanged, as the period of an oscillator does not depend on the mass.

questions.explanation: T = 2π√(m/k). Multiplying m by 4 multiplies √m by 2, so the period doubles. The period of SHM does not depend on the amplitude, so the change from A to 2A has no effect.

questions.stem: Two oscillators, P and Q, each have a time period of 0.80 s. Q reaches its maximum positive displacement 0.20 s after P does. What is the phase difference between P and Q, in radians?
questions.explanation: Q lags P by 0.20/0.80 = 0.25 of a cycle. One cycle is 2π rad, so the phase difference is 2π × 0.25 = π/2 = 1.57 rad.

questions.stem: A particle moves with simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of 0.080 m and a time period of 0.50 s. What is its speed when its displacement is 0.050 m?

The displacement of a particle moving with simple harmonic motion is x = x₀ sin(ωt + φ). At t = 0 the particle passes through its equilibrium position moving in the negative x-direction. What is the phase constant φ?

options.text: φ = 0 rad, as sin 0 = 0 and so the particle starts at equilibrium
φ = −π/2 rad, as moving in the negative direction makes x negative, so sin φ = −1
φ = π/2 rad, as cos(π/2) = 0 and the particle starts at equilibrium
φ = π rad, since sin π = 0 and x becomes negative just after t = 0

questions.explanation: At t = 0, x = x₀ sin φ = 0, so φ = 0 or π rad. The velocity is v = ωx₀ cos(ωt + φ); for motion in the negative direction cos φ must be negative, so φ = π rad. Just after t = 0, sin(ωt + π) is negative, as required.

questions.stem: A body of mass 0.40 kg moves with simple harmonic motion with angular frequency 5.0 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.12 m. What is its kinetic energy when its displacement is 0.060 m?

A particle moves with simple harmonic motion with a time period of 2.0 s and an amplitude of 0.050 m. At t = 0 it passes through its equilibrium position moving in the positive direction, so x = x₀ sin ωt. What is its displacement at t = 0.30 s?
